name: Paris: Capital of Revolutions, Light and Ideas
description: A river island, a cathedral and a university grew into the city that staged revolutions, world fairs, new painting and new philosophy.

checkpoints.name: Island, school and cathedral
checkpoints.note: Paris began as a settlement beside the Seine. The University of Paris grew up in the Middle Ages, and Notre-Dame, begun in the twelfth century and finished in the fourteenth, rose over the river island.

checkpoints.name: The court of the Sun King
checkpoints.note: Louis XIV made Versailles the home of his court and ruled France for decades. The palace showed the power of the crown, and its cost weighed on the kings who followed, down to Louis XVI.

checkpoints.name: Revolution and empire
checkpoints.note: In 1789 crowds took the Bastille and the French Revolution began. Louis XVI was executed, Robespierre led the Reign of Terror, and Napoleon rose from the chaos to rule France.

checkpoints.name: Fairs, painters and writers
checkpoints.note: Paris held great fairs, including the Exposition Universelle of 1855, 1889 and 1900, and built the Eiffel Tower. Monet and the Impressionists, Hugo, Curie, Debussy and the Lumiere brothers worked here, and the Dreyfus affair split the country.

checkpoints.name: Paris in the modern age
checkpoints.note: Picasso and the Cubists, Sartre and Simone de Beauvoir, and the filmmakers of the French New Wave made Paris a centre for art and ideas. Charles de Gaulle led France, and nations signed the Paris Agreement in 2015.
